race_context: Baugo Community Schools, known locally as Jimtown, serves the northwest corner of Elkhart County. It has four schools: Jimtown Elementary, Jimtown Intermediate, Jimtown Junior High and Jimtown High School. The superintendent is Byron Sanders, Ph.D. {baugo_home}{baugo_supt}.
In November 2025 Sanders told The Elkhart Truth that enrollment is about 1,800 with little fluctuation {et_contract25}.
The board has five members: Julie Phillips (president), Robert Barbour (vice president), Chris Carithers (secretary), Todd Hochstetler and Bill Gletty {baugo_board}.

Members must live in one of three residence districts. A 2023 district notice says the election plan requires a member to have lived in their district for at least a year {baugo_vacancy23}{et_2020}. In 2020 the ballot let voters choose up to two candidates, no more than one from any district; the county clerk said 379 votes were rejected because voters picked two candidates from the same district {et_2020}.

Seats on the 2026 ballot: one District I seat and the District III seats. In 2022 three members were elected: Julie Phillips in District 1, and Jamie Lee Wenger and Bill Gletty in District 3 {et_2022}. Those terms run through Dec. 31, 2026 {baugo_vacancy23}. The state candidate list shows District III as 'vote for 1', but both 2022 District 3 seats appear to be up, so the race may elect two members. Check the sample ballot {in_list}{et_2022}{baugo_vacancy23}.
District I: incumbent Julie Newcomer Phillips is unopposed {in_list}{baugo_board}.

District III: incumbent Bill Gletty, current board vice president Robert Barbour and former board member Jamie L Wenger are on the ballot {in_list}{baugo_board}. Wenger resigned his District 3 seat in September 2023, and the board took applications to appoint a District 3 resident for the rest of the term {baugo_vacancy23}.

Facilities and debt: on June 24, 2024 the board made a preliminary determination to issue about $28 million in bonds through a lease of up to 16 years. The money would pay for renovations and additions across the district, including safety and security, site and athletic improvements, equipment and technology. The district projected no net increase in the debt service tax rate as older debt matures {baugo_bond24}.
Staff pay: in November 2025 the board unanimously approved a teacher contract with a $1,000 raise for 2026-27, a $46,000 starting salary and a $78,000 top salary {et_contract25}.
No reporting was found on how the 2025 property-tax law (SEA 1) affects Baugo, or on any Baugo referendum plans.
No 2026 Baugo candidate forum, questionnaire or news coverage of the race was found.
